title: Beastgrid - Animal Collection and Tactical Battler Game
author: AlbadonCo
selftext:
I made an Animal Collection and battling game using Rosebud ai that is playable on both the rosebud website at https://rosebud.ai/d/d2f65c4f-a224-49a9-9a70-df84b59f3654 as well as on its standalone site at beastgrid.games.

I need more players to help me play test for balance adjustments as I only have 2 daily players not including myself currently. QoL suggestions are welcome, and feel free to give your favorite animal ideas to add to the game! (Mythical creatures included)

comments.author: AlbadonCo
comments.body: Also for insight, the game DOES play on mobile, but its mostly optimized for pc, so it is harder to read certain things or tap certain buttons. After logging in, you can go to the settings and turn on full screen which makes things a bit better!

comments.author: HippieYoHippieYay
comments.body:
Feedback: After clicking the 50th tutorial popup, I lost patience and quit the page. 

Few people will invest that much time for a generic AI browser game, especially one that looks based on 99% of mobile game bullshit (but that also doesn't work well on mobile?)

replies.author: AlbadonCo
replies.body:
Fair, but there is a skip button for a reason.

Also I simply have put less time into mobile optimization than other things at the moment. No worries

replies.author: HippieYoHippieYay
replies.body:
There is a tutorial skip but with such feature overload if you skip you are just hit with what I call "mobile game bullshit": blings and bongs, coins, achievements, way too many buttons in the menu, way too much text and overlapping features, etc. 

If you are actually serious: start the tutorial directly with a "tutorial battle" and not text popups. You need to first show the player why they should later care about the other filler stuff. Also avoid text like the plague, kids don't read and some are straight up illiterate.

replies.author: AlbadonCo
replies.body: I dont think its really as complicated as the long tutorial makes it seem, I definitely overdid it in fear of someone complaining they didnt get something. I feel like anyone could realistically figure everything out pretty easily. I could likely remove 90% of the tutorial and just give a basic run down

replies.author: HippieYoHippieYay
replies.body:
Maximize "show, don't tell", right now it's the opposite.

Don't forget that, as heartless as this might sound: when somebody launches your game for the first time they probably do not give a shit about it, at all. They got there because of a single small drop of curiosity but the slightest "friction" and most players will just skip to the next game, they don't lack choice in 2025.

You got somebody to click on your game which is already an achievement, so the first thing you do then is try to grab their attention and SHOW in an instant why they would want to stay, nobody will sit and read long tutorials for a vibe coded browser game and also nobody will sit and "figure it out" if they are not at all invested. 
It's either frictionless or the X button is a single click and your game is instantly erased from the player's memory, they won't come back.

replies.author: RemarkableGuidance44
replies.body: If you have to hold their hand you are building games wrong...

replies.author: AlbadonCo
replies.body: Understandable, I prefer to figure things out myself, and if it really takes that much effort to figure out would also assume poor design without proper guidance. Much less tutorial needed 🫡

comments.author: Significant_Task393
comments.body: It doesnt even load on mobile. This is the lowest AI slop effort

replies.author: AlbadonCo
replies.body: Not that im expecting you to boot it back up, but I did take into account what you said and optimized the loading at game start, which makes the game load faster all around, including on my phone, so your feedback was still helpful.
